81290.subject: Chemistry
81290.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A : Generally, $3d$ transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R : Involvement of $3d$-electrons in addition to $4s$-electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: $\text{A}$ is not correct but $\text{R}$ is correct.
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$.
Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\text{A}$.
$\text{A}$ is correct but $\text{R}$ is not correct.
81290.sol:
Assertion A is correct because transition metals generally have high melting points due to strong metallic bonding.

Reason R is correct and explains Assertion A because the strong metallic bonding in $3d$ transition metals is attributed to the involvement of a greater number of electrons from the $3d$ subshell in addition to the $4s$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.

Thus, both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both $\text{A}$ and $\text{R}$ are correct and $\text{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\text{A}$.

81743.subject: Chemistry
81743.text: What is the correct relationship between the $\mathrm{pHs}$ of isomolars solution of sodium oxide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_1\right)$, sodium sulphide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_2\right)$, sodium selenide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_3\right)$ and sodium telluruide $\left(\mathrm{pH}_4\right)$ ?
81743.sol:
It is given that the isomolar solutions are sodium salt of Group 16 elements are present in equal molar concentration. The salts on hydrolysis with water, it produces an acid and base, as follows:
I. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaOH}$
II. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S}$
III. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Se}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaOH}$ $+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$
IV. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Te}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}>2 \mathrm{NaOH}$ $+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
The acidic strength of the hydrides is in the order $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} < $ $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$, due to increase in the atomic size.
As the acidic character of the hydride increases down the group, the basic character of the salt decreases down the group. Therefore, the order of basic character of the salts will be: $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{O}>\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}>\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Se}>\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Te}$
Therefore, the order of $\mathrm{pH}$ of the given aqueous solution is $\mathrm{pH}_1>\mathrm{pH}_2>$ $\mathrm{pH}_3>\mathrm{pH}_4$
Related Theory
The $\mathrm{pH}$ of the isomolar solution, can be determined with respect to the basic character of the sodium salts of the Group 16 elements. These salts undergo hydrolysis, forming hydrides, whose acidic character can account for the basic character of the salt, formed through neutralisation.
A Caution
In the reverse reaction of neutralisation, from the acidic strength of the hydrides, we can obtain the order of ease of neutralisation of the sodium hydroxide with the hydrides. As more the acidity of the hydride, more will be the neutralisation to form the salt.

84353.subject: Zoology
84353.text: There are two opposing views about origin of modern man. According 10 one view Homo erectus in Asia were the ancestors of modern man. A study of variation of DNA however suggested African origin of modern man. What kind of observation on DNA variation could suggest this?
options: greater variation in Asia than in Africa
greater variation in Africa than in Asia
similar variation in Africa and Asia
variation only in Asia and no variation in Africa.
84353.sol:
There are two models about origin of modern man (Homo sapiens sapiens)
(i) Multiregional model: According to this view, modern humans evolved in many parts of the world from regional descendants of Homo erectus who dispersed from Africa between 1 and 2 million years ago.
(ii) Monogenesis model: According to this view, African descendents of Homo erectus gave rise to modern humans.
In late 1980s, Rebecca Cann and other geneticists supported this view on the basis of DNA of living humans. They compared the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) of a multiathenic sample of more than 100 people representing four continents. The greater the difference between the mtDNAs of two peoples, the longer ago that mtDNAs diverged from a common source. By using bioinformarics, they concluded that the divergence of mtDNA of Africans from common source began just 200, 000 years ago, much to late to represent the dispersal of Homo erectus. Thus, there are greater variation in Asia than in Africa.

95041.subject: Physics
95041.text: A man is standing on the platform and one train is approaching and another train is going away with the speed of $4ms^{- 1}$, frequency of sound produced by train is $240$ Hz. What will be the number of beats heard by him per second? (velocity of sound = $300ms^{- 1}$)
95041.sol:
The apparent frequency heard by the man is given by

${n}_{app} = n \left(\dfrac{v \pm {v}_{o}}{v \pm {v}_{s}}\right)

On our case,${v}_{o} = 0$

$∴ {n}_{app} = n $\left(\dfrac{v}{v \pm {v}_{s}}\right)$

Given, $v = 300ms^{- 1}, {v}_{s} = 4ms^{- 1}, n = 240Hz$

In the first case, the train is approaching the man, so frequency heard

${n}_{1} = n \left(\dfrac{v}{v \pm {v}_{s}}\right) =$240$\left(\dfrac{300}{300 - 4}\right)

$= $\dfrac{240 \times 300}{296} =$243.24$ Hz

In the second case, the train is going away from the man, so frequency heard

${n}_{2} = n $\left(\dfrac{v}{v + {v}_{s}}\right) = 240\left(\dfrac{300}{300 + 4}\right)$

$= \dfrac{240 \times 300}{304} = 236.84Hz$

Hence, the number of beats heard by the man per second

$= {n}_{1} - {n}_{2}$

$= 243.24 - 236.84 = 6.4 \approx 6$

96128.text: Who concluded from his studies that the presence of a cell wall is a unique feature of plant cells?
96128.sol: Theodore Schwann (1839), a British Zoologist, studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the ‘plasma membrane’. Cell division phase of cell cycle has two stages - karyokinesis and cytokinesis. Karyokinesis deals with nuclear division where at the end of this stage two nuclei are formed. Following karyokinesis, cytokinesis occurs where the cytoplasm is divided in two resulting in formation of two new whole individual cells. The given diagram represent the cytokinesis stage of plant cell division. In it, the division occurs by making a cell plate in the cytoplasm between the two newly formed nuclei which later becomes the cell wall of the new cell that will form.

Diakinesis is part of prophase I of meiosis I which is part of karyokinesis.

DNA synthesis is part of S -phase in interphase.

Interphase is the stage of cell cycle that occurs between two cell division processes.

96591.subject: Botany
96591.text: The productivity of the oceans is approximately _______ the annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere.
96591.sol: Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons. Thus 55 out of 170 is 32.35% which is around one third.

100500.subject: Physics
100500.text: A body of mass $m$ is projected from the ground with an initial kinetic energy $K$ at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the vertical. The kinetic energy of the body at the highest point of its trajectory will be
100500.sol:
Let the initial speed of the body be $u$. The initial kinetic energy is given by:
$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^2$

The angle of projection with the vertical is $30^{\circ}$. Therefore, the angle of projection with the horizontal is $\theta = 90^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.

At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of velocity is zero. The speed of the body is equal to the horizontal component of its initial velocity, which remains constant.

Speed at highest point, $v = u \cos 60^{\circ} = u \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{u}{2}$

The kinetic energy at the highest point is:
$K' = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(\dfrac{u}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}mu^2\right)$

$\Rightarrow K' = \dfrac{K}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{K}{4}$

100670.subject: Physics
100670.text: A block of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ is placed on a rough inclined plane which makes an angle of $37^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. It is connected by a light string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass $10 \text{ kg}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the $5 \text{ kg}$ block and the incline is $0.25$. Find the acceleration of the system when released from rest. (Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin 37^{\circ} = 0.6$, $\cos 37^{\circ} = 0.8$)
100670.sol:
Let the mass on the incline be $m_1 = 5 \text{ kg}$ and the hanging mass be $m_2 = 10 \text{ kg}$.

The driving force pulling the system is the weight of the hanging mass:
$W_2 = m_2 g = 10 \times 10 = 100 \text{ N}$.

The forces opposing the motion of the $5 \text{ kg}$ block up the incline are the component of its weight parallel to the incline and the kinetic friction.
Component of weight down the incline: $m_1 g \sin 37^{\circ} = 5 \times 10 \times 0.6 = 30 \text{ N}$.

The normal force on the block is $N = m_1 g \cos 37^{\circ} = 5 \times 10 \times 0.8 = 40 \text{ N}$.
The kinetic friction force is $f_k = \mu_k N = 0.25 \times 40 = 10 \text{ N}$.

The net force accelerating the system is:
$F_{\text{net}} = W_2 - m_1 g \sin 37^{\circ} - f_k$
$F_{\text{net}} = 100 - 30 - 10 = 60 \text{ N}$.

The total mass of the system is $m_1 + m_2 = 5 + 10 = 15 \text{ kg}$.

The acceleration of the system is:
$a = \dfrac{F_{\text{net}}}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac{60}{15} = 4.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Answer: $4.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$

100892.subject: Physics
100892.text: A block of mass $m$ is projected with an initial velocity $v_0$ on a rough horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface increases linearly with the distance $x$ from the starting point as $\mu_k = bx$, where $b$ is a positive constant. The distance $D$ at which the block comes to rest is :
100892.sol:
According to the Work-Energy Theorem, the net work done on the block equals its change in kinetic energy: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K$

The frictional force acting on the block at a distance $x$ is $f_k = \mu_k mg = bxmg$.

The work done by friction as the block moves from $x=0$ to $x=D$ is:

$W_f = \int_{0}^{D} (-f_k) dx = -\int_{0}^{D} bxmg dx = -bmg \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{D} = -\dfrac{1}{2}bmgD^2$

The change in kinetic energy is $\Delta K = K_f - K_i = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2$

Equating the two:

$-\dfrac{1}{2}bmgD^2 = -\dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2$

$bmgD^2 = mv_0^2$

$D^2 = \dfrac{v_0^2}{bg}$

$D = \dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt{bg}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt{bg}}$

101879.text: A lake is covered with a layer of ice under a steady sub-zero outside temperature. Let $t_1$ be the time taken for the thickness of the ice layer to increase from $1 \text{ cm}$ to $2 \text{ cm}$, and $t_2$ be the time taken for the thickness to increase from $2 \text{ cm}$ to $3 \text{ cm}$. The ratio $t_1 : t_2$ is
101879.sol:
The rate of heat conduction through an ice layer of thickness $x$ is given by $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{KA\theta}{x}$.

The heat released when a layer of thickness $dx$ freezes is $dQ = \rho A L dx$.

Equating the two, we get $\rho A L \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{KA\theta}{x} \Rightarrow dt = \dfrac{\rho L}{KA\theta} x dx$.

Integrating both sides, the time taken for the thickness to increase from $x_i$ to $x_f$ is $t = \dfrac{\rho L}{2KA\theta} (x_f^2 - x_i^2)$.

Thus, the time taken is proportional to the difference of the squares of the thicknesses.

For the first interval: $t_1 \propto (2^2 - 1^2) = 4 - 1 = 3$.

For the second interval: $t_2 \propto (3^2 - 2^2) = 9 - 4 = 5$.

Therefore, the ratio $t_1 : t_2$ is $3 : 5$.

Answer: $3 : 5$

102798.text:
Consider the following statements about electric dipoles and electric fields:
Statement-I: The electric field at a point on the axial line of an electric dipole is directed along the dipole moment vector.
Statement-II: The electric field at a point on the equatorial line of an electric dipole is directed opposite to the dipole moment vector.
Statement-III: The torque acting on an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is proportional to the dipole moment and the magnitude of the electric field.
Statement-IV: The potential due to an electric dipole at a point on the equatorial line is zero.
Choose the correct option:
options: Statement-I, Statement-III, and Statement-IV are true; Statement-II is false.
Statement-I, Statement-II, and Statement-III are true; Statement-IV is false.
Statement-II and Statement-IV are true; Statement-I and Statement-III are false.
102798.sol:
- Statement-I: This is true. The electric field at a point on the axial line of a dipole is along the direction of the dipole moment.
- Statement-II: This is true. The electric field at a point on the equatorial line of a dipole is directed opposite to the dipole moment vector.
- Statement-III: This is true. The torque \(\tau\) acting on a dipole in a uniform electric field is given by:
\(\tau=p E \sin \theta\)
- Statement-IV: This is false. The potential at a point on the equatorial line of a dipole is not zero, but it is given by:
\(V=\frac{p \cos \theta}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 r^2}\)

103520.subject: Physics
103520.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a diamagnetic material is placed in a non-uniform magnetic field, it tends to move from the stronger to the weaker part of the field.
Reason (R): The magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) of a diamagnetic material is small and positive.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
103520.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: Diamagnetic materials develop an induced magnetic moment in a direction opposite to the applied magnetic field. As a result, they are feebly repelled by magnets and tend to move from the stronger to the weaker part of a non-uniform magnetic field.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) of a diamagnetic material is small and negative ($-1 \le \chi < 0$). It is paramagnetic materials that have a small and positive susceptibility.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect

103908.subject: Physics
103908.text: A circular coil of $200$ turns and radius $0.1 \text{ m}$ is rotated at a constant angular velocity of $10 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$ in a uniform magnetic field of $0.5 \text{ T}$. If the electrical resistance of the coil is $10 \ \Omega$, what is the maximum external torque required to maintain this constant rotation?
103908.sol:
The area of the circular coil is $A = \pi r^2 = \pi (0.1)^2 = 0.01\pi \text{ m}^2$.

The maximum induced EMF is $\varepsilon_{\text{max}} = NAB\omega$.
$\varepsilon_{\text{max}} = 200 \times 0.01\pi \times 0.5 \times 10 = 10\pi \text{ V}$.

The maximum induced current in the coil is $I_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{\varepsilon_{\text{max}}}{R} = \dfrac{10\pi}{10} = \pi \text{ A}$.

To maintain constant rotation, the external torque must balance the opposing magnetic torque. The magnetic torque on the coil is $\tau = MB\sin\theta = (NIA)B\sin\theta$.

The maximum magnetic torque occurs when the current is maximum and $\sin\theta = 1$:
$\tau_{\text{max}} = N I_{\text{max}} A B$
$\tau_{\text{max}} = 200 \times \pi \times 0.01\pi \times 0.5 = \pi^2 \text{ N m}$.

Answer: $\pi^2 \text{ N m}$

104252.subject: Physics
104252.text: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum has an amplitude of $30\sqrt{2} \text{ V m}^{-1}$. The rms value of the oscillating magnetic field is: (Speed of light in vacuum $= 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$)
104252.sol:
Given:
Electric field amplitude, $E_0 = 30\sqrt{2} \text{ V m}^{-1}$
Speed of light, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

First, find the amplitude (peak value) of the magnetic field using the relation $c = \dfrac{E_0}{B_0}$:
$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{2}}{3 \times 10^8} = 10\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-8} \text{ T} = \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

Next, calculate the rms value of the magnetic field using $B_{rms} = \dfrac{B_0}{\sqrt{2}}$:
$B_{rms} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-7}}{\sqrt{2}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

Answer: $1.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

104287.subject: Physics
104287.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Wave Equation)List II (Direction of complementary field)
(A) $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t) \hat{i}$(I) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{k}$
(B) $\vec{B} = B_0 \cos(\omega t + ky) \hat{i}$(II) $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{i}$
(C) $\vec{E} = E_0 \cos(kx - \omega t) \hat{j}$(III) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$
(D) $\vec{B} = B_0 \sin(kz + \omega t) \hat{j}$(IV) $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{k}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104287.sol:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of the cross product $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

(A) $\vec{E}$ is along $\hat{i}$ and the wave propagates along $+z$ direction ($\hat{k}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{i} \times \hat{B} = \hat{k}$. Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$ (Matches III).

(B) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{i}$ and the wave propagates along $-y$ direction ($-\hat{j}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{E} \times \hat{i} = -\hat{j}$. Since $(-\hat{k}) \times \hat{i} = -\hat{j}$, $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{k}$ (Matches IV).

(C) $\vec{E}$ is along $\hat{j}$ and the wave propagates along $+x$ direction ($\hat{i}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{j} \times \hat{B} = \hat{i}$. Since $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$, $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{k}$ (Matches I).

(D) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$ and the wave propagates along $-z$ direction ($-\hat{k}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{E} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{k}$. Since $(-\hat{i}) \times \hat{j} = -\hat{k}$, $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{i}$ (Matches II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

104694.subject: Physics
104694.text: Two separate Young's double slit experiments are performed. In the first experiment, light of wavelength $500 \text{ nm}$ is used with a slit separation $d$ and screen distance $D$. In the second experiment, light of wavelength $600 \text{ nm}$ is used with a slit separation $\dfrac{d}{2}$ and screen distance $2D$. The ratio of the fringe width in the first experiment to that in the second experiment is
104694.sol:
Fringe width in a Young's double slit experiment is given by $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.

For the first experiment:
$\beta_1 = \dfrac{\lambda_1 D_1}{d_1} = \dfrac{500 \text{ nm} \times D}{d}$

For the second experiment:
$\beta_2 = \dfrac{\lambda_2 D_2}{d_2} = \dfrac{600 \text{ nm} \times (2D)}{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{2400 \text{ nm} \times D}{d}$

Taking the ratio of the two fringe widths:
$\dfrac{\beta_1}{\beta_2} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{500 D}{d}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{2400 D}{d}\right)} = \dfrac{500}{2400} = \dfrac{5}{24}$

Thus, the ratio is $5 : 24$.

Answer: $5 : 24$

108623.subject: Chemistry
108623.text: The standard enthalpy of solution of $\mathrm{AgCl}(s)$ is $+65 \mathrm{~kJ/mol}$. If the standard enthalpies of formation of $\mathrm{Ag}^+(aq)$ and $\mathrm{Cl}^-(aq)$ are $+105 \mathrm{~kJ/mol}$ and $-167 \mathrm{~kJ/mol}$ respectively, the standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{AgCl}(s)$ in $\mathrm{kJ/mol}$ is :
108623.sol:
The dissolution of silver chloride in water is represented by the equation:
$\mathrm{AgCl}(s) \rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}^+(aq) + \mathrm{Cl}^-(aq)$

According to Hess's Law, the standard enthalpy of solution is given by the difference between the sum of the standard enthalpies of formation of the products and the reactant:
$\Delta H_{sol}^\circ = [\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{Ag}^+) + \Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{Cl}^-)] - \Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{AgCl})$

Substituting the given values:
$+65 = [+105 + (-167)] - \Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{AgCl})$
$65 = -62 - \Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{AgCl})$

Rearranging to solve for the standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{AgCl}(s)$:
$\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{AgCl}) = -62 - 65 = -127 \mathrm{~kJ/mol}$

Answer: $-127$

109374.subject: Chemistry
109374.text: The solubility product ($K_{sp}$) of a sparingly soluble salt of the type $M_2X$ is $3.2 \times 10^{-11}$. What is the molar concentration of $M^+$ ions in its saturated aqueous solution?
109374.sol:
For a sparingly soluble salt of type $M_2X$, the dissociation equilibrium is:

$M_2X(s) \rightleftharpoons 2M^+(aq) + X^{2-}(aq)$

If the molar solubility of the salt is $s$, then at equilibrium:
$[M^+] = 2s$
$[X^{2-}] = s$

The solubility product $K_{sp}$ is given by:
$K_{sp} = [M^+]^2[X^{2-}] = (2s)^2(s) = 4s^3$

Given $K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11} = 32 \times 10^{-12}$:
$4s^3 = 32 \times 10^{-12}$
$s^3 = 8 \times 10^{-12}$
$s = (8 \times 10^{-12})^{1/3} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

The concentration of $M^+$ ions is:
$[M^+] = 2s = 2 \times (2 \times 10^{-4}) = 4.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Answer: $4.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Match List-I with List-II regarding the reactions of toluene.

(B) $\text{CrO}_3, (\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}$(II) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OCOCH}_3)_2$
(C) $\text{Cl}_2, h\nu$(III) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHCl}_2$

113881.subject: Chemistry
113881.text: When chlorobenzene and bromobenzene are mixed at constant temperature and pressure, which of the following sets of thermodynamic relations is correct for the resulting mixture?
113881.sol:
A mixture of chlorobenzene and bromobenzene forms an ideal solution because the intermolecular attractive forces between chlorobenzene and bromobenzene are nearly the same as those in the pure components.

For an ideal solution, the enthalpy of mixing and the volume of mixing are zero: $\Delta_{\text{mix}}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$.

Since the mixing of two miscible liquids is a spontaneous process, the Gibbs free energy of mixing must be negative ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}G < 0$) and the entropy of mixing must be positive ($\Delta_{\text{mix}}S > 0$).

Therefore, the correct set of relations is $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$ and $\Delta_{\text{mix}}G < 0$.

Answer: $\Delta_{\text{mix}}V = 0$, $\Delta_{\text{mix}}G < 0$

117072.subject: Chemistry
117072.text:
The standard electrode potentials $\left(\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\right)$ for the $\mathrm{M}^{2+} / \mathrm{M}$ couple of some $3d$ series elements are observed as follows: $\mathrm{V} (-1.18 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Cr} (-0.90 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Mn} (-1.18 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Fe} (-0.44 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Ni} (-0.25 \mathrm{V})$, $\mathrm{Cu} (+0.34 \mathrm{V})$, and $\mathrm{Zn} (-0.76 \mathrm{V})$.

While the general trend across the series is that the $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value becomes less negative, $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ break this trend by exhibiting more negative values than expected. Which of the following statements correctly explains this anomaly?
options: $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ have exceptionally high enthalpies of atomisation compared to other transition metals.
The hydration enthalpies of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ are exceptionally high, making their formation highly favourable.

The formation of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ is thermodynamically favoured due to their stable exactly half-filled $\left(d^5\right)$ and fully-filled $\left(d^{10}\right)$ configurations respectively.
$\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ achieve stability by attaining $d^4$ and $d^9$ electronic configurations respectively.
117072.sol:
The standard electrode potential $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{M}^{2+} / \mathrm{M}\right)$ depends on the sum of the enthalpy of atomisation, ionisation enthalpies ($\Delta_i \mathrm{H}_1 + \Delta_i \mathrm{H}_2$), and hydration enthalpy.

Across the $3d$ series, the general trend is a less negative $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value due to the general increase in the sum of the first and second ionisation enthalpies.

However, $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ have more negative $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ values than the trend predicts. This is because the $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ion has a stable exactly half-filled $3d^5$ configuration, and the $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ ion has a stable fully-filled $3d^{10}$ configuration.

The extra thermodynamic stability of these configurations lowers the required ionisation energy to form the $+2$ state, making the overall $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value more negative. The other options are incorrect: $\mathrm{Mn}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}$ actually have low enthalpies of atomisation, and their configurations are $d^5$ and $d^{10}$, not $d^4$ and $d^9$.

Answer: The formation of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ is thermodynamically favoured due to their stable exactly half-filled $\left(d^5\right)$ and fully-filled $\left(d^{10}\right)$ configurations respectively.

117084.subject: Chemistry
117084.text:
Read the following statements regarding the melting points and metallic bonding of $d$-block elements:
(A) The high melting points of transition metals are attributed to the involvement of only $(n-1)d$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
(B) In any transition series, the melting point generally rises to a maximum at $d^{5}$ configuration.
(C) Zinc, cadmium and mercury are hard metals with high melting points.
(D) The strength of the metallic bond decreases as the number of unpaired $d$-electrons increases.

How many of the above statements are correct?
117084.sol:
Statement (A) is incorrect. According to NCERT, the high melting points of transition metals are attributed to the involvement of a greater number of electrons from the $(n-1)d$ subshell in addition to the $ns$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.

Statement (B) is correct. In any transition series, the melting point generally rises to a maximum at $d^{5}$ configuration (except for anomalous values of $\text{Mn}$ and $\text{Tc}$) and then falls regularly as the atomic number increases.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Zinc, cadmium and mercury have fully filled $d$-subshells ($d^{10}$) and their $d$-electrons do not participate in metallic bonding. Hence, they are soft metals with exceptionally low melting points.

Statement (D) is incorrect. The strength of the metallic bond increases as the number of unpaired $d$-electrons increases, which leads to higher enthalpies of atomisation and melting points.

Therefore, only one statement (B) is correct.

Answer: Only one

119294.subject: Chemistry
119294.text: An $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone, 3-ethyl-4-methylhex-3-en-2-one, is formed as one of the products when a mixture of two carbonyl compounds is heated with dilute $\text{NaOH}$. Which of the following pairs of reactants can undergo cross-aldol condensation to yield this product?
119294.sol:
The given product is an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone formed by aldol condensation. To find the reactant carbonyl compounds, we perform a retro-aldol analysis by cleaving the $\text{C=C}$ double bond.

The structure of 3-ethyl-4-methylhex-3-en-2-one is:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{C}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$

Cleaving the double bond between C3 and C4:
- Add two hydrogen atoms to the $\alpha$-carbon (C3) to get the enolate precursor: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (Pentan-2-one).
- Add an oxygen atom with a double bond to the $\beta$-carbon (C4) to get the electrophilic precursor: $\text{O=C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (Butan-2-one).

Thus, the reactants are pentan-2-one and butan-2-one. Choosing pentan-3-one or propanal would lead to incorrect alkyl branching in the final product.

Answer: Pentan-2-one and Butan-2-one

(b) All cyanobacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts.
(c) Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidize various inorganic substances to produce ATP.
(d) Slime moulds form a plasmodium under unfavourable conditions.
(e) Mycoplasma are pathogenic to animals but not to plants.

How many of the above statements are correct?
121567.sol:
Let us evaluate each statement based on NCERT facts:

(a) Correct: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission.
(b) Incorrect: Not all, but only 'some' cyanobacteria (like Nostoc and Anabaena) can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called heterocysts.
(c) Correct: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidize inorganic substances (such as nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia) and use the released energy for ATP production.
(d) Incorrect: Slime moulds form an aggregation called plasmodium under 'suitable' (favourable) conditions. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips.
(e) Incorrect: Many mycoplasma are pathogenic to both animals and plants, not just animals.

Only statements (a) and (c) are correct. Therefore, the total number of correct statements is two.

Answer: Two

121702.subject: Botany
121702.text: What type of gametes are involved in oogamous reproduction?
options: One large, non-motile and one small, motile gamete
Two gametes of the same size and type
121702.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. <mark>Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous,</mark> e.g., Volvox, Fucus

121750.subject: Botany
121750.text: In which type of habitat are the majority of red algae found?
121750.sol: The members of rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. <mark>Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas.</mark> They occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular. Some of them have complex body organization. The food is stored as floridean starch which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure. The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation. They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. Sexual reproduction is oogamous and accompanied by complex post fertilization developments. The common members are: Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria and Gelidium.

123017.text: A plant has flowers with a bicarpellary, syncarpous, superior ovary that is bilocular with a swollen placenta. Which of the following correctly represents the floral formula symbol for this gynoecium and its corresponding placentation type?
123017.sol:

123028.subject: Botany
123028.text:
Consider the following three plants:
(i) Mustard
(ii) Peach
(iii) Guava

Select the correct sequence of terms describing the position of the ovary in the flowers of these plants, respectively.
123028.sol:
In mustard, the flower is hypogynous, meaning the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior.

In peach, the flower is perigynous, meaning the gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level. The ovary here is said to be half-inferior.

In guava, the flower is epigynous, where the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it. The ovary is said to be inferior.

Thus, the correct sequence is Superior, Half-inferior, Inferior.

Answer: Superior, Half-inferior, Inferior

125224.subject: Botany
125224.text: During which stage in the complete oxidation of glucose are the greatest number of ATP molecules formed from ADP?
options: Conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl Co-A
125224.sol:
In glycolysis 4 ATP and $2 \mathrm{NADH}_2$ molecules are formed. These $2 \mathrm{NADH}_2$ molecules go to electron transport chain.
In oxidative decarboxylation no ATP molecule is formed but two molecules of $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ are formed from two molecules of pyruvate. These two $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ go to electron transport chain. In Krebs cycle 2 ATP, $6 \mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $2 \mathrm{FADH}_2$ molecules are formed from two molecule of acetyl Co-A. These $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $\mathrm{FADH}_2$ go to electron transport chain. In electron transport chain all $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $\mathrm{FADH}_2$ pass to electron carriers and yield 3 ATP and 2 ATP molecules per $\mathrm{NADH}_2$ and $\mathrm{FADH}_2$ respectively.
Thus,
4 ATP are formed in glycolysis
2 ATP in Krebs cycle and
34 ATP from electron transport chain
40 ATP
2 ATP molecules are used during glycolysis.
So, net gain of ATP molecules during one complete oxidation of a glucose molecule is 38 ATP.

125861.subject: Botany
125861.text: How many nuclei are formed after the first mitotic division of the functional megaspore?
125861.sol: Let us study about the formation of the embryo sac in detail The nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically to form two nuclei which move to the opposite poles, forming the 2- nucleate embryo sac. Two more sequential mitotic nuclear divisions result in the formation of the 4-nucleate and later the 8-nucleate stages of the embryo sac. It is of interest to note that these mitotic divisions are strictly free nuclear, that is, nuclear divisions are not followed immediately by cell wall formation. After the 8-nucleate stage, cell walls are laid down leading to the organisation of the typical female gametophyte or embryo sac. Observe the distribution of cells inside the embryo sac Six of the eight nuclei are surrounded by cell walls and organised into cells; the remaining two nuclei, called polar nuclei are situated below the egg apparatus in the large central cell. There is a characteristic distribution of the cells within the embryo sac.

127150.subject: Botany
127150.text: What percentage of total species have been recorded according to May's global estimates?
127150.sol: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world. Nearly 45,000 species of plants and twice as many of animals have been recorded from India. How many living species are actually there waiting to be discovered and named? If we accept May’s global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. Applying this proportion to India’s diversity figures, we estimate that there are probably more than 1,00,000 plant species and more than 3,00,000 animal species yet to be discovered and described

127250.subject: Botany

127250.sol: Let us look at some interesting aspects about earth’s biodiversity based on the currently available species inventories. More than 70 per cent of all the species recorded are animals, while plants (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms) comprise no more than 22 percent of the total. Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than 70 per cent of the total. That means, out of every 10 animals on this planet, 7 are insects. Again, how do we explain this enormous diversification of insects? The number of fungi species in the world is more than the combined total of the species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals. 127975.subject: Zoology
127975.text: Which structure in the frog's brain is unpaired?
127975.sol: The system for control and coordination is highly evolved in the frog. It includes both neural system and endocrine glands. The chemical coordination of various organs of the body is achieved by hormones which are secreted by the endocrine glands. The prominent endocrine glands found in frog are pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, pineal body, pancreatic islets, adrenals and gonads. The nervous system is organised into a central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), a peripheral nervous system (cranial and spinal nerves) and an autonomic nervous system (sympathetic and parasympathetic). There are ten pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain. Brain is enclosed in a bony structure called brain box (cranium). The brain is divided into fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain. Forebrain includes olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres and unpaired diencephalon. The midbrain is characterised by a pair of optic lobes. Hind-brain consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata. The medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum and continues into spinal cord, which is enclosed in the vertebral column

128125.subject: Zoology
128125.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Male frogs can be easily distinguished from female frogs externally.
Reason (R): Male frogs possess sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
128125.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because frogs exhibit clear sexual dimorphism, allowing males and females to be distinguished externally.

Reason (R) is true because male frogs have specific external morphological features, namely sound-producing vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs, which are absent in female frogs.

Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A) as these specific structures are the exact criteria used for external distinction between the sexes. Therefore, both statements are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

128290.sol: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism. The disease is hard to diagnose in the early stages and often goes undetected for many years, until changes in external features become noticeable. Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them. TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland. ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex. LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins. In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of hormones called androgens from testis. In males, FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis. 128338.subject: Zoology
128338.text: What are the two hormones secreted by the adrenal medulla?
128338.sol: The adrenal medulla secretes two hormones called adrenaline or epinephrine and noradrenaline or norepinephrine. These are commonly called as catecholamines. Adrenaline and noradrenaline are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergency situations and are called emergency hormones or hormones of Fight or Flight. These hormones increase alertness, pupilary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs), sweating etc. Both the hormones increase the heart beat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration.Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis; and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids. Cortisol is also involved in maintaining the cardio-vascular system as well as the kidney functions. Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response. Cortisol stimulates the RBC production. Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of Na+ and water and excretion of K+ and phosphate ions. Thus, aldosterone helps in the maintenance of electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure.Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex which play a role in the growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.
128338.meta: What are the two hormones secreted by the adrenal medulla?

128356.subject: Zoology
128356.text: What is the main role of glucagon in our body?
options: Maintenance of normal blood glucose levels
128356.sol: Glucagon is a peptide hormone, and plays an important role in maintaining the normal blood glucose levels. Glucagon acts mainly on the liver cells (hepatocytes) and stimulates glycogenolysis resulting in an increased blood sugar (hyperglycemia). In addition, this hormone stimulates the process of gluconeogenesis which also contributes to hyperglycemia. Glucagon reduces the cellular glucose uptake and utilisation. Thus, glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone.Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to a complex disorder called diabetes mellitus which is associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of harmful compounds known as ketone bodies. Diabetic patients are successfully treated with insulin therapy.
128356.meta: What is the main role of glucagon in our body?

128384.subject: Zoology
128384.text: What hormone is secreted by the atrial wall of the heart?
128384.sol: Now you know about the endocrine glands and their hormones. However, as mentioned earlier, hormones are also secreted by some tissues which are not endocrine glands. For example, the atrial wall of our heart secretes a very important peptide hormone called atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which decreases blood pressure. When blood pressure is increased, ANF is secreted which causes dilation of the blood vessels. This reduces the blood pressure.Endocrine cells present in different parts of the gastro-intestinal tract secrete four major peptide hormones, namely gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin (CCK) and gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP). Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively. GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility. Several other non-endocrine tissues secrete hormones called growth factors. These factors are essential for the normal growth of tissues and their repairing/regeneration. Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors (present in the nucleus). Binding of a hormone to its receptor leads to the formation of a hormone-receptor complex

128613.subject: Zoology
128613.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

(A)Pars distalis(I)Secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(B)Pars intermedia(II)Produces releasing hormones
(C)Pars nervosa(III)Stores and releases oxytocin
(D)Hypothalamus(IV)Secretes prolactin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
128613.sol:
Pars distalis (anterior pituitary) secretes hormones such as prolactin, growth hormone, TSH, ACTH, LH, and FSH.

Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH).

Pars nervosa (posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, but does not synthesise them.

The hypothalamus produces releasing and inhibitory hormones, and also synthesises oxytocin and vasopressin which are transported axonally to the pars nervosa.

Thus, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II).

129170.subject: Zoology
129170.text: What is coordination in the context of organ systems in the human body?
options: A system that regulates the function of muscles and blood vessels.
The process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions.
A system that regulates the endocrine system.
A system that regulates the neural system.
129170.sol: Coordination refers to the process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions in order to maintain homeostasis. When physical exercise is performed, the supply of oxygen increases to meet the increased energy demand. When physical exercise is stopped, the activities of nerves, lungs, heart and kidney gradually return to their normal conditions. The neural system and the endocrine system jointly coordinate and integrate all the activities of the organs so that they function in a synchronised fashion. The neural system provides an organized network of point-to-point connections for quick coordination. The endocrine system provides chemical integration through hormones.

129530.subject: Zoology
129530.text: What is the function of Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) in urine formation?
options: Maintenance of high osmolarity of medullary interstitial fluid
Reabsorption of essential nutrients, electrolytes and water
Conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water
Maintenance of pH and ionic balance of body fluids
129530.sol: Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT): PCT is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium which increases the surface area for reabsorption. Nearly all of the essential nutrients, and 70-80 percent of electrolytes and water are reabsorbed by this segment. PCT also helps to maintain the pH and ionic balance of the body fluids by selective secretion of hydrogen ions and ammonia into the filtrate and by absorption of HCO3– from it. Henle’s Loop: Reabsorption is minimum in its ascending limb. However, this region plays a significant role in the maintenance of high osmolarity of medullary interstitial fluid. The descending limb of loop of Henle is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. This concentrates the filtrate as it moves down.

129826.subject: Zoology
129826.text: How many times does a healthy human breathe per minute on average?
129826.sol: The contraction of external inter-costal muscles lifts up the ribs and the sternum causing an increase in the volume of the thoracic chamber in the dorso-ventral axis.The overall increase in the thoracic volume causes a similar increase in pulmonary volume. An increase in pulmonary volume decreases the intra-pulmonary pressure to less than the atmospheric pressure which forces the air from outside to move into the lungs, i.e., inspiration. Relaxation of the diaphragm and the inter-costal muscles returns the diaphragm and sternum to their normal positions and reduce the thoracic volume and thereby the pulmonary volume.This leads to an increase in intra-pulmonary pressure to slightly above the atmospheric pressure causing the expulsion of air from the lungs, i.e., expiration. We have the ability to increase the strength of inspiration and expiration with the help of additional muscles in the abdomen. On an average, a healthy human breathes 12-16 times/minute. The volume of air involved in breathing movements can be estimated by using a spirometer which helps in clinicalassessment of pulmonary functions.

131793.subject: Zoology
131793.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The genetic code is considered nearly universal, but exceptions exist in mitochondrial codons and some protozoans.
Reason (R): Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, which makes the genetic code degenerate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
131793.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: The genetic code is nearly universal (for example, from bacteria to human, UUU would code for Phenylalanine), but NCERT explicitly notes that there are some exceptions to this rule in mitochondrial codons and in some protozoans.

Reason (R) is true: Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, and this property is known as the degeneracy of the genetic code.

Both statements are factually correct and represent independent properties of the genetic code. However, the degeneracy of the code is not the reason why there are exceptions to its universality. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

132246.subject: Zoology
132246.text: Which category of genetic disorders involves alterations or mutations in a single gene?
132246.sol: Broadly, genetic disorders may be grouped into two categories – Mendelian disorders and Chromosomal disorders. Mendelian disorders are mainly determined by alteration or mutation in the single gene. These disorders are transmitted to the offspring on the same lines as we have studied in the principle of inheritance. The pattern of inheritance of such Mendelian disorders can be traced in a family by the pedigree analysis. Most common and prevalent Mendelian disorders are Haemophilia, Cystic fibrosis, Sicklecell anaemia, Colour blindness, Phenylketonuria, Thalassemia, etc. It is important to mention here that such Mendelian disorders may be dominant or recessive. By pedigree analysis one can easily understand whether the trait in question is dominant or recessive. Similarly, the trait may also be linked to the sex chromosome as in case of haemophilia. It is evident that this X-linked recessive trait shows transmission from carrier female to male progeny

132451.subject: Zoology
132451.text:
In a certain monohybrid cross, the $F_1$ offspring exhibit a phenotype that does not resemble either of the two parents and is intermediate between them. Upon selfing of these $F_1$ individuals, the $F_2$ generation produces a phenotypic ratio that is exactly identical to its genotypic ratio (1:2:1).

Which of the following examples best represents this genetic phenomenon?
132451.sol:
The phenomenon described is incomplete dominance, where the $F_1$ phenotype is intermediate between the two parents and does not resemble either of them completely. In incomplete dominance, the $F_2$ phenotypic ratio is 1:2:1, which is identical to the genotypic ratio.

Flower colour in dog flower (Antirrhinum) is a classic example of incomplete dominance.

ABO blood grouping is an example of co-dominance and multiple allelism. Skin colour in humans is an example of polygenic inheritance, which shows continuous variation. Phenylketonuria is an example of pleiotropy, where a single gene affects multiple traits.

Answer: Flower colour in dog flower

132472.subject: Zoology
132472.text: Consider a normal male grasshopper and a normal male peacock. Which of the following correctly describes the sex chromosomal composition of the sperms produced by them?
options: The grasshopper produces 50% sperms with an X chromosome and 50% with a Y chromosome, while the peacock produces 100% sperms with a Z chromosome.
The grasshopper produces 50% sperms with an X chromosome and 50% with no sex chromosome, while the peacock produces 50% sperms with a Z chromosome and 50% with a W chromosome.
Both the grasshopper and the peacock produce two different types of sperms, exhibiting male heterogamety.
The grasshopper produces 50% sperms with an X chromosome and 50% with no sex chromosome, while the peacock produces 100% sperms with a Z chromosome.
132472.sol:
The grasshopper follows the XX-XO mechanism of sex determination. A normal male grasshopper has an XO sex chromosome constitution. During spermatogenesis, 50% of the sperms receive an X chromosome and the other 50% receive no sex chromosome.

The peacock (a bird) follows the ZW-ZZ mechanism of sex determination. A normal male peacock has a ZZ sex chromosome constitution (male homogamety). Therefore, 100% of the sperms produced by a male peacock will carry a Z chromosome.

Thus, the grasshopper exhibits male heterogamety by producing two types of sperms, while the peacock exhibits male homogamety by producing only one type of sperm.

Answer: The grasshopper produces 50% sperms with an X chromosome and 50% with no sex chromosome, while the peacock produces 100% sperms with a Z chromosome.

133011.subject: Zoology
133011.text: Which one of the following are analogous structures?
options: Wings of Bat and Wings of Pigeon
Gills of Prawn and Lungs of Man
Flippers of Dolphin and legs of Horse.
133011.sol:
Analogous structures are those organs which are structurally different, but they perform the same set of functions. Of the given pairs of structures, the gills of prawns and lungs of man are analogous in nature. Both of these are respiratory structures, which are anatomically different from each others. The lungs of man are balloon-like sac organs which inflate and deflate on breathing, while gills of prawn are crescent-shaped organs which perform gas exchange for respiration.

Wings of bat and wings of pigeon have anatomically similar structures as well as they perform the same function of flying. Hence, it is difficult to strictly mark them as analogous or homologous.

The other two examples exhibit homology. That is, they are structurally the same, but they perform different functions.

To create a system where the insects are kept at manageable levels through a complex system of checks and balances within a living and vibrant ecosystem

A genetic engineer wants to recover a very high number of copies (e.g., 1000 copies per cell) of a target alien DNA. To achieve this, the alien DNA must be cloned into a suitable vector.

The 'ori' sequence controls the copy number, and the 'rop' gene codes for the replication proteins.
The selectable marker controls the copy number, and the 'rop' gene codes for the replication proteins.
The 'ori' sequence controls the copy number, and the $amp^{R}$ gene codes for the replication proteins.
134792.sol:
According to NCERT, the origin of replication ('ori') is a sequence from where replication starts. This sequence is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA. Therefore, to recover many copies of the target DNA, it should be cloned in a vector whose origin supports a high copy number.

The 'rop' gene codes for the proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid.

Thus, the 'ori' sequence controls the copy number, and the 'rop' gene codes for the replication proteins.

Answer: The 'ori' sequence controls the copy number, and the 'rop' gene codes for the replication proteins.

135054.subject: Zoology
135054.text: What does the size of a population indicate about its status in the habitat?
135054.sol: <mark>The size of the population tells us a lot about its status in the habitat</mark>. Whatever ecological processes we wish to investigate in a population, be it the outcome of competition with another species, the impact of a predator or the effect of a pesticide application, we always evaluate them in terms of any change in the population size. The size, in nature, could be as low as <10 (Siberian cranes at Bharatpur wetlands in any year) or go into millions (Chlamydomonas in a pond). Population size, technically called population density (designated as N), need not necessarily be measured in numbers only. Although total number is generally the most appropriate measure of population density, it is in some cases either meaningless or difficult to determine

135107.subject: Zoology
135107.text: What type of evolutionary research is highlighted as currently important?
options: Evolution of physical adaptations to extreme environments
Evolution of life history traits in different species
Evolution of behavioral traits in animals
135107.sol: Populations evolve to maximize their reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness (high r value), in the habitat in which they live. Under a particular set of selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy. Some organisms breed only once in their lifetime (Pacific salmon fish, bamboo) while others breed many times during their lifetime (most birds and mammals). Some produce a large number of small-sized offspring (Oysters, pelagic fishes) while others produce a small number of large-sized offspring (birds, mammals). So, which is desirable for maximizing fitness? Ecologists suggest that life history traits of organisms have evolved in relation to the constraints imposed by the abiotic and biotic components of the habitat in which they live. <mark>Evolution of life history traits in different species is currently an important area of research being conducted by ecologists</mark>.

If the determinant of the matrix ${\left({P}^{- 1}AP - {I}_{3}\right)}^{2}$ is $\alpha{\omega}^{2}$, then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to _________.
301555.sol:
Let $M = {\left({P}^{- 1}AP - I\right)}^{2}$

$= {\left({P}^{- 1}AP\right)}^{2} - 2{P}^{- 1}AP + I$

$= {P}^{- 1}{A}^{2}P - 2{P}^{- 1}AP + I$

$PM = {A}^{2}P - 2AP + P$

$= \left({A}^{2} - 2A . I + {I}^{2}\right)P$

$⇒ Det \left(PM\right) = Det \left({\left(A - I\right)}^{2} \times P\right)$

$⇒ Det \left(PM\right) = = Det {\left(A - I\right)}^{2} \times Det \left(P\right)$

$⇒ DetM = = {\left(Det\left(A - I\right)\right)}^{2}$

Now $A - I = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 7 & {w}^{2} \\ - 1 & - w - 1 & 1 \\ 0 & - w & - w\end{cases}\right]$

$Det \left(A - I\right) = \left({w}^{2} + w + w\right) + 7\left(- w\right) + {w}^{3} = - 6w$

$Det {\left(\left(A - I\right)\right)}^{2} = 36{w}^{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 36$

$⇒ Ε = BRv$

The total force exerted by the limb on the monkey is the resultant of the normal force and the frictional force.

Since the normal force and frictional force are perpendicular to each other, the magnitude of the total force $F$ is given by:

$F = \sqrt{N^2 + f^2}$

Substituting the given values $N = 48 \text{ N}$ and $f = 20 \text{ N}$:

$F = \sqrt{48^2 + 20^2}$

$F = \sqrt{2304 + 400}$

$F = \sqrt{2704} = 52 \text{ N}$

303684.text: Three equal masses $m$ are located at the three corners of an equilateral triangle of side $a$. Evaluate the force exerted by this arrangement on an additional particle of mass $m$ placed at the centre of the triangle.
303684.sol:
Let the three masses be placed at the vertices A, B, and C of the equilateral triangle, and the additional mass be placed at the centroid O.

The gravitational force exerted by the mass at A on the mass at O is $\vec{F}_A$ directed along OA. Similarly, the forces due to the masses at B and C are $\vec{F}_B$ and $\vec{F}_C$ directed along OB and OC respectively.

Since the triangle is equilateral, the distances from the centroid to the vertices are equal, i.e., $OA = OB = OC$. Therefore, the magnitudes of the three forces are equal:

$|\vec{F}_A| = |\vec{F}_B| = |\vec{F}_C| = F$

The angle between any two of these force vectors is $120^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$.

The resultant of $\vec{F}_B$ and $\vec{F}_C$ has a magnitude of $\sqrt{F^2 + F^2 + 2F^2 \cos(120^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}})} = F$ and is directed opposite to $\vec{F}_A$.

Thus, the net gravitational force on the particle at the centre is $\vec{F}_{net} = \vec{F}_A + \vec{F}_B + \vec{F}_C = 0$.

303747.text: In a double slit interference experiment, a source emits light of wavelengths $480 \text{ nm}$ and $600 \text{ nm}$. The separation between the slits is $0.25 \text{ mm}$, and the interference is observed on a screen placed at $150 \text{ cm}$ from the slits. Determine the linear separation between the first maximum (adjacent to the central maximum) corresponding to the two wavelengths.
303747.sol:
The position of the $n$-th maximum in a double slit interference pattern is given by $y_n = \dfrac{n \lambda D}{d}$.

For the first maximum adjacent to the central maximum, $n = 1$. The position is $y = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$.

The linear separation between the first maxima corresponding to the two wavelengths $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ is:

$\Delta y = y_2 - y_1 = \dfrac{(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1) D}{d}$

Given values are:

$\lambda_1 = 480 \text{ nm} = 480 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$

$\lambda_2 = 600 \text{ nm} = 600 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$

$D = 150 \text{ cm} = 1.5 \text{ m}$

$d = 0.25 \text{ mm} = 0.25 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$

Substituting these values into the expression for $\Delta y$:

$\Delta y = \dfrac{(600 - 480) \times 10^{-9} \times 1.5}{0.25 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\Delta y = \dfrac{120 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.5}{0.25 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\Delta y = \dfrac{180 \times 10^{-9}}{0.25 \times 10^{-3}}$

$\Delta y = 720 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$

$\Delta y = 0.72 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m} = 0.72 \text{ mm}$

304667.chapter: Wave Motion and Waves on a String
304667.text: Two waves having an equal amplitude $A$ and the same frequency propagate in the same direction within a medium. The amplitude of the resultant wave is
304667.sol:
Let the two waves be $y_1 = A \sin(\omega t - kx)$ and $y_2 = A \sin(\omega t - kx + \phi)$.

By the principle of superposition, the amplitude of the resultant wave is given by $A_R = \sqrt{A_1^2 + A_2^2 + 2A_1A_2\cos\phi}$.

Substituting $A_1 = A_2 = A$, we get $A_R = \sqrt{A^2 + A^2 + 2A^2\cos\phi} = \sqrt{2A^2(1+\cos\phi)}$.

Using the trigonometric identity $1+\cos\phi = 2\cos^2 $\$left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right), we get $A_R = 2A\left|\cos\$left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\right|.

Since the phase difference $\phi$ is not specified, it can take any value.

The maximum amplitude occurs when $\cos\$left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) = \pm$1$, giving $A_\max = 2A$.

The minimum amplitude occurs when $\cos\$left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) =$0$, giving $A_\min = 0$.

Thus, the amplitude of the resultant wave lies between $0$ and $2A$.$

305035.chapter: Bohr's Model and Physics of the Atom
305035.text: A hydrogen atom initially in the $n = 6$ state undergoes two successive transitions to reach the ground state. During the first transition, a photon of $1.13 \text{ eV}$ is emitted. What is the value of $n$ for the intermediate state?
305035.sol:
Energy of an electron in the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by $E_n = -\dfrac{13.6}{n^2} \text{ eV}$.

For the initial state $n = 6$, the energy is $E_6 = -\dfrac{13.6}{6^2} = -0.377 \text{ eV}$.

During the first transition, a photon of energy $1.13 \text{ eV}$ is emitted. The energy of the intermediate state $n'$ is $E_{n'} = E_6 - 1.13 \text{ eV}$.

$E_{n'} = -0.377 - 1.13 = -1.507 \text{ eV}$.

Equating this to the energy formula for the $n'$-th state:

$-\dfrac{13.6}{n'^2} = -1.507$

$n'^2 = \dfrac{13.6}{1.507} \approx 9$

$n' = 3$

The intermediate state is $n = 3$.

305135.text: In the circuit shown in the figure, every capacitor has a capacitance of $10 \mu\text{F}$. The battery provides an emf of $100 \text{ V}$. Determine the energy stored in each of the four capacitors.
options: $16 \text{ mJ}$ in (a) and (d), $4 \text{ mJ}$ in (b) and (c)
$8 \text{ mJ}$ in (a) and (d), $2 \text{ mJ}$ in (b) and (c)
$2 \text{ mJ}$ in (a) and (d), $8 \text{ mJ}$ in (b) and (c)
$4 \text{ mJ}$ in (a) and (d), $4 \text{ mJ}$ in (b) and (c)
305135.sol:
From the given circuit, capacitors $b$ and $c$ are connected in parallel, and their combination is in series with capacitors $a$ and $d$.

The equivalent capacitance of $b$ and $c$ is:
$C_{bc} = C_b + C_c = 10\mu\text{F} + 10\mu\text{F} = 20\mu\text{F}$

The total equivalent capacitance of the circuit $C_{eq}$ is:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{C_a} + \dfrac{1}{C_{bc}} + \dfrac{1}{C_d}$

$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{5}{20}\mu\textF^{-1}$

$C_{eq} = 4\mu\text{F}$

The total charge supplied by the battery is:
$Q = C_{eq}V = 4\mu\text{F} \times 100\text{ V} = 400\mu\text{C}$

Since capacitors $a$ and $d$ are in series with the main circuit, the charge on each is:
$Q_a = Q_d = 400\mu\text{C}$

Since capacitors $b$ and $c$ are in parallel and have equal capacitance, the total charge splits equally between them:
$Q_b = Q_c = \dfrac{400\mu\text{C}}{2} = 200\mu\text{C}$

The energy stored in a capacitor is given by $U = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C}$.

Energy stored in capacitors $a$ and $d$:
$U_a = U_d = \dfrac{(400 \times 10^{-6})^2}{2 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{160000 \times 10^{-12}}{20 \times 10^{-6}} = 8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J} = 8\text{ mJ}$

Energy stored in capacitors $b$ and $c$:
$U_b = U_c = \dfrac{(200 \times 10^{-6})^2}{2 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{40000 \times 10^{-12}}{20 \times 10^{-6}} = 2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J} = 2\text{ mJ}$

Answer: $8 \text{ mJ}$ in (a) and (d), $2 \text{ mJ}$ in (b) and (c)

305159.text: A capacitor of capacitance $5.00 \mu\text{F}$ is charged to $24.0 \text{ V}$, while a second capacitor of capacitance $6.0 \mu\text{F}$ is charged to $12.0 \text{ V}$. The positive plate of the first capacitor is subsequently connected to the negative plate of the second, and vice versa. Determine the loss of electrostatic energy during this process.
305159.sol:
When the positive plate of the first capacitor is connected to the negative plate of the second, the common potential $V$ is given by:

$V = \dfrac{C_1 V_1 - C_2 V_2}{C_1 + C_2}$

The loss of electrostatic energy during this process is given by the formula:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} (V_1 + V_2)^2$

Substituting the given values $C_1 = 5.00 \mu\text{F}$, $C_2 = 6.0 \mu\text{F}$, $V_1 = 24.0 \text{ V}$, and $V_2 = 12.0 \text{ V}$:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{5.00 \times 6.0}{5.00 + 6.0} \times (24.0 + 12.0)^2 \mu\text{J}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{30.0}{11.0} \times (36.0)^2 \mu\text{J}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{15}{11} \times 1296 \mu\text{J}$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{19440}{11} \mu\text{J} \approx 1767.27 \mu\text{J}$

$\Delta U \approx 1.77 \text{ mJ}$

305205.text: A wire of length $4 \text{ m}$ and cross-sectional area $1 \text{ mm}^2$ carries a current of $2 \text{ A}$. Given that the material holds $10^{29}$ free electrons per cubic metre, determine the average time required for an electron to traverse the entire length of the wire.
305205.sol:
The drift velocity of free electrons is given by the relation $I = n e A v_d$, which gives $v_d = \dfrac{I}{n e A}$.

The average time required for an electron to traverse the length $L$ of the wire is $t = \dfrac{L}{v_d} = \dfrac{L n e A}{I}$.

Substituting the given values:
$L = 4 \text{ m}$
$n = 10^{29} \text{ m}^{-3}$
$e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$
$A = 1 \text{ mm}^2 = 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$
$I = 2 \text{ A}$

$t = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{29} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 10^{-6}}{2}$

$t = \dfrac{6.4 \times 10^4}{2}$

$t = 3.2 \times 10^4 \text{ s}$

305246.text: Determine the value of $R$ in the figure such that the current flowing through it is zero.
305246.sol:
The given circuit is a Wheatstone bridge.

The condition for zero current through the central resistor $R$ is that the bridge must be balanced.

Checking the ratio of resistances of the arms:

$\dfrac{10}{10} = 1$

$\dfrac{5}{5} = 1$

Since the ratios are equal, the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, the potential difference across the central resistor is zero, so no current flows through it regardless of its resistance.

Therefore, $R$ can have any value.

305522.subject: Physics
305522.text: A rectangular wire-frame of width $d$, mass $m$, and resistance $R$ has a large length. As shown in the figure, a uniform magnetic field $B$ is present to the left of the frame. At $t = 0$, a constant force $F$ begins pushing the frame into the magnetic field region. Determine the acceleration of the frame once its speed reaches $v$.
305522.sol:
When the rectangular wire-frame enters the magnetic field with velocity $v$, an induced motional emf is generated in its leading edge of length $d$.

The induced emf is given by:
$\varepsilon = Bvd$

The induced current in the frame is:
$I = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{R} = \dfrac{Bvd}{R}$

This current flowing through the leading edge experiences a magnetic force opposing the motion of the frame (according to Lenz's law). The magnitude of this magnetic force is:
$F_m = IdB = \left(\dfrac{Bvd}{R}\right)dB = \dfrac{B^2 d^2 v}{R}$

The net force acting on the frame is the applied force $F$ minus the opposing magnetic force $F_m$:
$F_{net} = F - F_m = F - \dfrac{B^2 d^2 v}{R}$

Using Newton's second law, the acceleration $a$ of the frame is:
$a = \dfrac{F_{net}}{m} = \dfrac{F - \dfrac{B^2 d^2 v}{R}}{m}$

$a = \dfrac{RF - v d^2 B^2}{mR}$

305939.chapter: Magnetic Field due to a Current
305939.text: Four long, straight wires, each carrying a current of $5.0 \text{ A}$, are arranged in a plane. Their points of intersection create a square with a side length of $5.0 \text{ cm}$, with centre $P$. Points $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, and $Q_4$ are located on the diagonals of this square at a distance from $P$ equal to the length of the square's diagonal, as shown in the figure. Determine the magnetic fields at these four points.
305939.sol:
Let the centre of the square be the origin $(0,0)$. The side length of the square is $a = 5.0 \text{ cm} = 0.05 \text{ m}$.

The four wires are located at $x = -a/2$, $x = a/2$, $y = -a/2$, and $y = a/2$. The currents are $I = 5.0 \text{ A}$ in the $+y$ direction for the vertical wires and in the $+x$ direction for the horizontal wires.

The diagonal of the square is $d = a\sqrt{2}$. The points $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3, Q_4$ are at a distance $d$ from the origin along the diagonals. Their coordinates are:
$Q_1 = (-a, a)$
$Q_2 = (a, a)$
$Q_3 = (a, -a)$
$Q_4 = (-a, -a)$

The magnetic field due to a long straight wire is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$.

At $Q_1(-a, a)$:
Field due to wire at $y = a/2$: $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi (a - a/2)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$ ($\odot$)
Field due to wire at $y = -a/2$: $B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi (a - (-a/2))} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{3\pi a}$ ($\odot$)
Field due to wire at $x = -a/2$: $B_3 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi |-a - (-a/2)|} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$ ($\odot$)
Field due to wire at $x = a/2$: $B_4 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi |-a - a/2|} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{3\pi a}$ ($\odot$)
Total field at $Q_1$: $B_{Q1} = B_1 + B_2 + B_3 + B_4 = \dfrac{8\mu_0 I}{3\pi a}$ ($\odot$)
Substituting the values: $B_{Q1} = \dfrac{8 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 5}{3\pi \times 0.05} = 1.067 \times 10^{-4} \text{ T} \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-4} \text{ T}$ ($\odot$)

At $Q_2(a, a)$:
Fields from horizontal wires are $\odot$ with magnitudes $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$ and $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{3\pi a}$.
Fields from vertical wires are $\otimes$ with magnitudes $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{3\pi a}$ and $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$.

At $Q_4(-a, -a)$:
Fields from horizontal wires are $\otimes$ with magnitudes $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{3\pi a}$ and $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$.

306061.text: A metal has a work function of $2.5 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$. Determine the threshold frequency for photoelectric emission.
306061.sol:
The work function of a metal is related to its threshold frequency by the equation $\Phi = h u_0$, where $h$ is Planck's constant and $ u_0$ is the threshold frequency.

Substituting the given values:

$ u_0 = \dfrac{\Phi}{h}$

$ u_0 = \dfrac{2.5 imes 10^{-19}}{6.63 imes 10^{-34}}$

$ u_0 \approx 3.77 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}$

Rounding to one decimal place, $ u_0 \approx 3.8 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}$

306121.subject: Physics
306121.text: Every resistance shown in the figure has a value of $20 \Omega$. Determine the equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$. Does this value depend on whether point $A$ or $B$ is at a higher potential?
306121.sol:
The given circuit can be analyzed as a Wheatstone bridge.

Let the junction between the top two resistors be $C$ and the junction between the bottom two resistors be $D$. The diode is connected between $C$ and $D$.

The resistance of each resistor is $20 \Omega$.
The ratio of resistances in the left arms is $\dfrac{20}{20} = 1$, and the ratio in the right arms is also $\dfrac{20}{20} = 1$.

Since the ratios are equal, the Wheatstone bridge is balanced. Therefore, the potential at point $C$ is equal to the potential at point $D$ ($V_C = V_D$).

Because there is no potential difference across the diode ($V_C - V_D = 0$), no current flows through the middle branch. This condition remains true regardless of whether point $A$ or point $B$ is at a higher potential.

Since the diode branch carries no current, it can be removed from the circuit for the purpose of calculating the equivalent resistance. The circuit then simplifies to two parallel branches:
Resistance of the upper branch $= 20 \Omega + 20 \Omega = 40 \Omega$
Resistance of the lower branch $= 20 \Omega + 20 \Omega = 40 \Omega$

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ between $A$ and $B$ is the parallel combination of these two branches:
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{40 \times 40}{40 + 40} = 20 \Omega$

This value is independent of the polarity of the applied voltage.

306331.subject: Physics
306331.chapter: Thermal and Chemical Effects of Electric Current
306331.text: A coil with a resistance of $100 \Omega$ is connected across a battery having an emf of $6.0 \text{ V}$. Assuming all the heat developed in the coil goes into raising its temperature, and given that the heat capacity of the coil is $4.0 \text{ J K}^{-1}$, determine the time required to increase the temperature of the coil by $15^{}^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C}$.
306331.sol:
The power generated by the coil is given by $P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}$.

Substituting $V = 6.0 \text{ V}$ and $R = 100 \Omega$, we get:

$P = \dfrac{(6.0)^2}{100} = 0.36 \text{ J s}^{-1}$

The heat required to raise the temperature of the coil is $Q = C \Delta T$.

Substituting $C = 4.0 \text{ J K}^{-1}$ and $\Delta T = 15^{}^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} = 15 \text{ K}$, we get:

$Q = 4.0 \times 15 = 60 \text{ J}$

The time required to generate this heat is $t = \dfrac{Q}{P}$.

$t = \dfrac{60}{0.36} = \dfrac{1000}{6} \text{ s}$

Converting the time into minutes:

$t = \dfrac{1000}{6 \times 60} = \dfrac{100}{36} = 2.77 \text{ minutes}$

Rounding off to one decimal place, the time required is $2.8 \text{ minutes}$.

306356.subject: Physics
306356.text: Calculate the cutoff wavelength of the continuous X-rays produced by an X-ray tube operating at $30 \text{ kV}$.
306356.sol:
The cutoff wavelength of continuous X-rays is given by the Duane-Hunt law:

$\lambda_{\text\min} = \dfrac{hc}{eV}$

Substituting the standard value $hc \approx 1242 \text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}$ and $V = 30 \text{ kV} = 30000 \text{ V}$:

$\lambda_{\text\min} = \dfrac{1242 \text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}}{30000 \text{ eV}}$

$\lambda_{\text\min} = 0.0414 \text{ nm}$

Since $1 \text{ nm} = 1000 \text{ pm}$:

$\lambda_{\text\min} = 41.4 \text{ pm}$

306598.subject: Physics
306598.text: Within a $p$-$n$ junction, the drift current is directed
options: from the $n$-side towards the $p$-side when the junction is forward-biased, and in the reverse direction when it is reverse-biased
from the $p$-side towards the $n$-side when the junction is forward-biased, and in the reverse direction when it is reverse-biased
306598.sol:
In a $p$-$n$ junction, the depletion region contains uncovered positive donor ions on the $n$-side and negative acceptor ions on the $p$-side.

This charge distribution creates an internal electric field directed from the $n$-side towards the $p$-side.

The drift current is caused by the movement of minority charge carriers under the influence of this built-in electric field. Holes (minority carriers on the $n$-side) are swept towards the $p$-side, and electrons (minority carriers on the $p$-side) are swept towards the $n$-side.

The flow of positive charges from $n$ to $p$ and negative charges from $p$ to $n$ both contribute to a conventional current directed from the $n$-side to the $p$-side.

The direction of this drift current is independent of the external biasing.

309560.subject: Chemistry
309560.text: Identify the correct decreasing order of acidic strength for the indicated hydroxyl protons (i), (ii), and (iii) in the following compound:
309560.sol:
The acidic strength of a hydroxyl proton depends on the stability of its conjugate base.

Deprotonation of the hydroxyl group (ii) yields a conjugate base where the negative charge on the oxygen is in conjugation with the $C=C$ double bond and the $C=O$ group. The resonance allows the negative charge to be delocalized onto the electronegative carbonyl oxygen ($O^{-} - C=C - C=O \rightarrow O=C - C^{-} - C=O \rightarrow O=C - C=C - O^{-}$). This extensive resonance stabilization makes (ii) the most acidic proton.

Deprotonation of the hydroxyl group (i) forms a conjugate base where the negative charge can delocalize over the $C=C$ double bond ($O^{-} - C=C \rightarrow O=C - C^{-}$), but it cannot delocalize onto the carbonyl oxygen. As it is an enolic group, it is moderately acidic but less acidic than (ii).

Deprotonation of the hydroxyl group (iii) forms an alkoxide ion on an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon. This conjugate base lacks resonance stabilization and is stabilized only by the inductive effect of the adjacent carbonyl group. Therefore, it is the least acidic.

Thus, the correct decreasing order of acidic strength is $(ii) > (i) > (iii)$
